title: A base test timeout counts as an assertion failure in screening verify
body:
evals/units/screening.ts one() records baseFailure 'assertion' whenever the base test is non-zero and not a compile failure, so a base test killed by its timeout (exit 124) counts as red by assertion and verified() accepts the unit. On 2026-11-17 the t-zk8cmrz first pass under load ~100 recorded testBase 124 for 5 units (t-1jr2vwd, t-1c4dlg5, t-1ynhv0n, t-1mwsacc, t-2f3cc85); the committed manifest holds t-2blfi57 verified with testBase 124.
Outcome: a base or fix test that exits 124 records a timeout verdict that verified() rejects (or triggers one sequential re-grade), and t-2blfi57 is re-graded on a quiet host so its base fails by assertion.
Proof: a unit test where the base test exits 124 is not verified; verify --recorded still prints >= 70.
